name: Shackleton Crater Rim
science_focus: Permanently shadowed terrain, polar impact processes, Peaks of Eternal Light
heritage: LRO LOLA / LROC / LEND remote sensing
notes: Rim site at the exact pole; illumination and direct-to-Earth geometry are both strongly terrain- and libration-sensitive.

name: Nobile Crater Rim / Connecting Ridge
region: Artemis candidate region, lunar South Pole
science_focus: Polar highlands, PSR access, Artemis landing-site geology
heritage: Artemis III candidate region studies; LRO LOLA / LROC
notes: Rolling ridge terrain between Nobile and Connecting Ridge; commonly assessed for polar landing and ISRU access.

name: Von Kármán Crater
region: South Pole–Aitken Basin, lunar far side
science_focus: Deep crust/mantle material in SPA, Chang'e-4 ground truth, far-side geology
heritage: Chang'e-4 / Yutu-2 landed in Von Kármán (2019)
notes: Far-side site: direct Earth line-of-sight is impossible; continuous communications require a relay.

name: Marius Hills
science_focus: Lunar volcanism, domes, sinuous rilles, lava-tube skylights
heritage: LROC / Kaguya Terrain Camera / Clementine / M3
notes: Flat basaltic plains intermixed with constructional domes, rilles, and collapse pits.

name: Vallis Schröteri & Cobra Head
science_focus: Largest sinuous rille, Cobra Head vent, young Aristarchus ejecta
notes: Extreme local relief: rille walls and cliffs exceed 1 km; the exact site is just outside the available UCL Aristarchus 10 m DTM footprint.

name: Apollo 17 — Taurus-Littrow Valley
science_focus: Ground-truth calibration, sample context, valley geology, surface operations
heritage: Apollo 17 crewed landing (1972); extensive surface photography and traverses
notes: Best ground-truthed site in the set; valley floor is bounded by the North and South Massifs.
